title.narrative: Eliminating hazardous chemicals from the supply chain of the construction sector in Morocco

description.narrative: Health improvements and reduced exposure to hazardous chemicals: The project will enhance public health by minimizing exposure to hazardous chemicals in construction materials. Through stricter regulations, safer material alternatives, and better waste management practices, the project will reduce respiratory diseases, skin conditions, and long-term health risks associated with toxic substances in construction. Creation of sustainable livelihoods: By promoting green construction and circular economy practices, the project will generate new economic opportunities in sustainable building materials, waste recycling, and eco-friendly construction techniques. Support for SMEs, especially women-led enterprises, will foster entrepreneurship and local job creation, strengthening community resilience. Economic empowerment through access to green finance: The project will improve access to green financing for SMEs and local businesses, enabling investments in innovative, sustainable materials and technologies. This will strengthen market competitiveness and promote long-term economic growth while reducing environmental impacts. Capacity building for long-term resilience: Targeted capacity-building activities will equip stakeholders – including construction companies, planners, and government officials – with the skills needed to adopt sustainable construction practices. These efforts will improve regulatory compliance, enhance resource efficiency, and support the development of climate-resilient infrastructure. Improved resource efficiency and circular economy integration: The project’s focus on life-cycle approaches and circular economy principles will reduce resource consumption, minimize waste, and promote material reuse. This will lower construction costs, conserve natural resources, and contribute to the long-term sustainability of the sector. Enhanced environmental and community resilience: By reducing environmental degradation, promoting sustainable urban planning, and improving waste management, the project will bolster community resilience to environmental shocks. Cleaner, safer environments will contribute to improved quality of life, particularly for vulnerable populations in urban and peri-urban areas. Support for local development priorities: The project aligns with Morocco’s national development goals, including sustainable urbanization, climate action, and social inclusion. By fostering public-private partnerships and supporting regulatory frameworks, the project will help achieve long-term socio-economic stability and equitable growth across regions. Promotion of equitable growth: With gender-responsive approaches integrated throughout, the project will promote equitable development by ensuring that women, youth, and marginalized groups benefit from new economic opportunities, capacity-building initiatives, and financial mechanisms. This inclusive approach will contribute to social cohesion and long-term stability. Behavioral change for sustainable practices: Through targeted awareness campaigns and educational programs, the project will encourage communities, policymakers, and private sector actors to adopt sustainable construction practices. This behavioral shift will support long-lasting environmental benefits and socio-economic gains. Long-term economic value through green innovation: By fostering innovation in green building materials and techniques, the project will create long-term economic value, reducing Morocco’s reliance on imported materials and strengthening local industries. Sustainable construction practices will reduce operational costs and improve the durability of infrastructure, benefiting both public and private sectors
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To promote a green transformation of the construction supply chain by replacing resource-intensive and hazardous materials with environmentally sound alternatives and promoting circular approaches and regenerative designs across the entire supply chain.
